A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RC research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy experiments on four LLMs and four datasets, coherence evaluations, and detailed results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a correctness diagnostic, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, and manual validation of the coherence judge.

M1.justification: RC-D and RC-S retain the same answer grouping, activation representations, similarity calculations, and frequency-weighted selection procedure. Negative weights appear only as experimental ablations, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CSQA, HellaSwag, MedMCQA, and MMLU. The new diagnostics reuse existing tasks and responses; open-ended generation and transfer across LLMs are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: NE, SC, and RC-E remain the comparison methods. The new Table 3's Embedding baseline explicitly uses the existing RC-E entailment calculation from Equation 11, rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols select correct-versus-incorrect answer groups with six responses each, sweep lambda from -1 to 1 across layers, and manually check ten examples with three responses per answer. The original tuning/test split, generation settings, models, and response budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supporting analyses: Table 3 controls answer frequency to examine correctness information in representations; Appendix D tests weight and layer sensitivity, including negative-weight controls; Appendix E adds manual judge validation and an illustrative MMLU case. These analyses are absent from v1.

E5.justification: The standard deviations across prompt-sample configurations in Appendix C.1 are retained. v2 adds no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its new findings.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and coherence results remain unchanged, but substantial diagnostic results are added. Table 3 reports correct-group consistency preferences of 53.3–58.4% for internal representations versus 47.8–50.9% for external entailment. Figures 7–10 add sensitivity curves, and Appendix E reports judge agreement on all ten manually labelled examples.

T1.justification: Appendix D introduces a limited mathematical extension for negative-lambda ablations: lambda times consistency plus (1 - |lambda|) times frequency. The original formal task and method definitions in Equations 1–12 remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusions retain the same contributions: activation-based answer aggregation, dense and sparse variants, accuracy improvements up to 4%, and alignment between sparse consistency and coherence. New analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the controlled diagnostic as evidence of useful information beyond textual outputs and explains behavior at extreme positive and negative weights. It also cautions that judging coherence may become harder with larger response sets and explicitly discusses open-ended and cross-model extensions.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds technical information about SAE overhead: one forward pass on a single-token activation, its input shape, and an approximately 0.1B-parameter SAE example. Existing implementation instructions, prompt templates, hardware information, and code/access references are retained.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including work on heterogeneous ensembles, activation transfer, and reward-model evaluation. These supplement related work, future directions, and coherence-judge justification without changing RC's central novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v2 adds localized explanations and appendix sections, expands future-work discussion, and moves Impact Statements from Appendix D to F. Author affiliation and conference-status text are also updated.

P2.justification: A new diagnostic table and four multi-panel sensitivity figures substantially expand the visual presentation. Table 2 is reformatted and relocated, and subsequent tables are renumbered. Existing Figures 1–6 and their reported results are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 3 better isolates representation information from answer frequency, while Appendix D exposes tuning sensitivity and failure modes missing from v1's evidence. The cost explanation and manual judge check also help assess the method. These provide a clear but limited strengthening: the judge validation covers only ten examples and adds no uncertainty analysis.
